title: Leveraging GPT-4 to transform chemistry from paper to practice

metadata.authors: Zhang W.; Guy M.A.; Yang J.; Hao L.; Liu J.; Hawkins J.M.; Mustakis J.; Monfette S.; Hein J.E.

abstract:
Leveraging GPT-4 to transform chemistry from
paper to practice†
Wenyu Zhang,
a Mason A. Guy,a Jerrica Yang,a Lucy Hao,a Junliang Liu,b
Joel M. Hawkins,c Jason Mustakis,
c Sebastien Monfette
*c
and Jason E. Hein
*abde
Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized numerous industries as well as accelerated scientiﬁc
research. However, their application in planning and conducting experimental science, has been limited.
In this study, we introduce an adaptable prompt-set with GPT-4, converting literature experimental
procedures into actionable experimental steps for a Mettler Toledo EasyMax automated laboratory
reactor. Through prompt engineering, we developed a 2-step sequential prompt: the ﬁrst prompt
converts literature synthesis procedures into step-by-step instructions for reaction planning; the second
prompt generates an XML script to communicate these instructions to the EasyMax reactor, automating
experimental design and execution. We successfully automated the reproduction of three distinct
literature-based synthetic procedures and validated the reactions by monitoring and characterizing the
products. This approach bridges the gap between text-to-procedure transcription and automated
execution, and streamlines literature procedure reproduction.

methods.value: Developing a two-step sequential prompt approach to transcribe literature procedures into step-by-step instructions and XML scripts, utilizing GPT-4's capabilities.

problems.value: The challenge of translating literature experimental procedures into actionable steps for automated laboratory reactors.

hypotheses.value: A two-step sequential prompt using GPT-4 can convert literature synthesis procedures into executable XML scripts for an automated laboratory reactor.

evidence.value: Successful automation of three distinct literature-based synthetic procedures, validated by monitoring and characterizing the products using online HPLC and NMR spectroscopy.

conclusions.value: The approach bridges the gap between text-to-procedure transcription and automated execution, streamlining literature procedure reproduction.

entities.value: Mettler Toledo EasyMax automated laboratory reactor

measurements.value: Successful automation of three distinct literature-based synthetic procedures, validated by monitoring and characterizing the products using online HPLC and NMR spectroscopy.

failure_paths.value: failure: Translation of lengthy protocols exceeding the token limit of GPT models. Evidence: Lengthy protocols need to be broken down into smaller portions due to token limit issues.

partial: GPT-4's accuracy in molecular weight lookup for chemical compounds. Evidence: GPT-4 showed 100% accuracy in density lookup but failed to output the correct molecular weight for 5,6-dichloropyrazine-2,3-dicarbonitrile in all conversations.
